statement: High-pressure hot-water washing (Exxon Valdez, Prince William Sound): hardshell clam (littleneck) abundance at washed sites was 92-97% below oiled, unwashed sites at 1, 2, 3 and 5 years after treatment (rows B018-B021, grade B, observational, treatment chosen by responders; B019 n = 3 vs 4 stations). Macroinfauna abundance and richness were also lower (B014-B016).
source: literature_effects.csv B014-B022; Houghton JP et al. (1996) NOAA Tech. Memo. NOS ORCA 91 (docs/reference/literature/Houghton_1996_PWS_Biology_ORCA91.pdf, opened this session); tables 4-6 to 4-9 exist in the report

statement: Littleneck clams at hot-water-washed sites needed until 2000 (11 years after the spill) to converge with unoiled sites, because washing winnowed fine sediment (row B024; abstract-only extraction, recovery-time ratio 3.67, no variance).
source: literature_effects.csv B024; Fukuyama AK, Shigenaka G, Coats DA (2014) Mar. Pollut. Bull. 84:56-69, doi:10.1016/j.marpolbul.2014.05.043 (publisher page did not open here; value taken from the owner-checked row)

statement: Exxon Valdez oil persists in the subsurface of Prince William Sound gravel beaches: field data and modelling indicate some oil was trapped in the anoxic lower layers of a two-layer beach when the water table was low; remediation was stopped in 1992 on the assumption of fast natural loss.
source: Li H, Boufadel MC (2010) Nature Geoscience, doi:10.1038/ngeo749 (abstract opened this session)

topic: persistence; natural recovery vs sediment relocation
statement: Svalbard field trials on mixed pebble-sand beaches: at a low-wave-energy site both natural attenuation and sediment relocation (surf washing) reduced residual oil and sediment toxicity in under five days; at a higher-energy site oil stranded above normal wave action behaved differently (the rest of the abstract was not opened).
source: Owens EH et al. (2003) USGS publication 70025441, https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/70025441 (abstract opened this session, truncated)

statement: NOAA guidance: oil penetration up to about 50 cm; oil tends to persist at and above the high-tide line where waves only occasionally reach; behaves like a sand beach if the sand fraction exceeds about 40 percent; asphalt pavements can form in sheltered pockets.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats p.28 (opened)

statement: NOAA guidance: deep penetration because of high permeability; rapid burial at high-tide and storm berms; persistence controlled by the depth of routine wave reworking; asphalt pavements likely along sheltered portions where accumulations are heavy.
source: NOAA OR&R (2017) Characteristic Coastal Habitats p.31 (opened)

statement: Surface washing agent applied to an Exxon Valdez gravel beach: hardshell clam density fell 75% overnight (row B054, grade C, before-after, one study, no variance).
source: literature_effects.csv B054; Lees DC, Houghton JP, Driskell WB (1993)
